a large proportion of the UK dog population is protected from cpv and CAV for many years after their primary vaccinations and that the protective antibody levels to these diseases in the adult dog population were higher than those of the vaccinated puppies.

a large proportion of adult dogs in the UK are protected against canine parvoviral enteritis, canine distemper and canine adenoviral hepatitis, despite not having been vaccinated for at last three years, and that the prevalence of protective antibody titres does not decrease with increasing length of time since the last vaccination.

the prevalence of protective antibodies to CPV and CAV in adult dogs that have not been vaccinated for up to 15 years is higher than that in dogs that have been vaccinated recently and that booster vaccination of adult dogs increases antibody titres to CAV but not to cpv or CDV.
